title: ESTune: Bayesian Uncertainty-Guided Early Stopping for Database Configuration Tuning
note: Bayesian early stopping for database configuration tuning - ML-based tuning of a system - local DBMS only - concern: no repo located

title: ApproxCaliper: A Programmable Framework for Application-aware Neural Network Optimization
note: Framework that prunes and quantizes networks against application-level goals rather than accuracy alone - the optimization pipeline runs on one GPU - concern - two of the case studies are a commercial agriculture robot and an electric-cart simulation so the application-level feedback loop may not be fully reproducible

title: BASE: Bridging the Gap between Cost and Latency for Query Optimization
note: RL query optimizer bridging cost and latency on PostgreSQL; same footprint as Bao/Lero, single node

title: DrGPUM: Guiding Memory Optimization for GPU-Accelerated Applications
note: GPU memory profiler built on CUPTI - single GPU user space no root or perf counters  GitHub + Zenodo artifact

title: Garnet: A Next-Generation Cache-Store for Accelerating Applications and Services
note: Redis-compatible cache-store rethought for thread scalability durability and transactions; mature open-source .NET artifact that runs on one node

title: Wait and See: A Delayed Transactions Partitioning Approach in Deterministic Database Systems for Better Performance
note: Batch transaction partitioning/scheduling in a deterministic database; concern - shared-nothing design, evaluated with partitions that can be colocated

title: Fast and Scalable Data Transfer Across Data Systems
note: Configurable data-transfer pipeline framework between data systems; can be run as processes on one host

title: DRAMHiT: A Hash Table Architected for the Speed of DRAM
note: User-space concurrent hash table built around software prefetching and batching; artifact evaluated, repo still active, has an AMD setup script. Serious concern - scripts/setup_amd.sh pins CPU frequency, enables explicit hugepages and disables hardware prefetchers, all of which need root or MSR access that is unavailable here; the reported numbers may not reproduce without them, so a scaled-down comparison would have to be justified.

title: VertexSurge: Variable Length Graph Pattern Match on Billion-edge Graphs
note: Single-machine C++/TBB engine for variable-length graph pattern matching; builds with cmake and user-space libraries. Concern - billion-edge LDBC datasets need a lot of RAM and disk, so a smaller scale factor may be necessary.

title: QServe:W4A8KV4 Quantization and System Co-design for Efficient LLM Serving
note: W4A8KV4 quantization with co-designed GPU kernels - INT4/INT8 Tensor Cores exist on Ampere (no FP8 needed) and 7-8B models fit 24 GB - concern: paper headline results use A100/L40S, and the repo is shared with LServe

title: Efficient and Portable Einstein Summation in SQL
note: Compiles Einstein-summation tensor expressions into portable SQL and runs them in a relational engine - a CPU-only single-node tensor runtime. Concern: contribution is a query-compilation technique rather than an ML runtime; no official repo found in GitHub or web search

title: Mirage: A Multi-Level Superoptimizer for Tensor Programs
note: Single-GPU tensor-program superoptimizer, mature public repo, Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concern: the search plus Z3 probabilistic equivalence check is CPU/GPU heavy and some generated kernels target A100/H100 feature levels - expect to re-tune for sm_86 and 24 GB.

title: Memento Filter: A Fast, Dynamic, and Robust Range Filter
note: Range filter data structure for LSM key-value stores; user-space C++

title: PLM4NDV: Minimizing Data Access for Number of Distinct Values Estimation with Pre-trained Language Models
note: Pre-trained language model used as a learned estimator inside the DBMS; code released by ByteDance

title: HotRAP: Hot Record Retention and Promotion for LSM-trees with Tiered Storage
note: RocksDB-based LSM-tree with hot-record promotion on tiered storage; evaluated on one 8-vCPU instance with a fast NVMe plus a slow disk. Concern: the slow tier was AWS gp3 and would have to be emulated on the local NVMe

title: Robustness of Updatable Learning-based Index Advisors against Poisoning Attack
note: Poisoning robustness of learning-based index advisors - a learned component inside a DBMS; PostgreSQL in user space is enough

title: OBASE: Object-Based Address-Space Engineering to Improve Memory Tiering
note: Compiler + user-space runtime that reorganises the virtual address space so pages become uniformly hot or cold - user-space memory management, no kernel changes. Concern: the paper's testbed has a real slow tier (Optane PMEM); this machine is one NUMA node with no PMEM/CXL, so a second tier would have to be emulated (cgroup limits + NVMe swap/zswap), which changes the measurement

title: Randomized Sketches for Quantile in LSM-tree based Store
note: Pre-computed randomized sketches stored in LSM components; user-space KV store change

title: Kitty: Accurate and Efficient 2-bit KV Cache Quantization with Dynamic Channel-wise Precision Boost
note: 2-bit KV quantization with dynamic channel-wise precision boost, page-centric layout and Triton dequantization kernels; single GPU and released code. Triton on CUDA 12.x wheels over driver 535 is the only setup risk worth flagging

title: Basilisk: Using Provenance Invariants to Automate Proofs of Undecidable Protocols
note: Dafny-based invariant-inference tool; artifact is pure user-space CPU software (Dafny 4.2 installs into $HOME) and the 16 protocol benchmarks are self-contained. Concern: it is a formal-methods paper, so an "improvement" would target inference coverage or proof time rather than a runtime system; Dafny/Z3 proof runs can be long on 16 threads.

title: LSGraph: A Locality-centric High-performance Streaming Graph Engine
note: Shared-memory streaming-graph engine (hierarchical indexed representation + locality-aware update). Single-machine multicore C++, competitors Terrace/Aspen/PaC-tree are also open source, so head-to-head comparison is cheap. Concern - the largest graphs used are multi-hundred-GB on disk; smaller SNAP graphs are a fine scale-down

title: Tiaccoon: Unified Access Control with Multiple Transports in Container Networks
note: Go middleware that hooks socket-API system calls and transparently substitutes a faster transport while keeping one access-control policy - a user-space syscall-interposition artifact, and the UNIX-domain-socket fast path plus the policy engine are testable on one host. Borderline, kept per the "note the concern" rule. Concern: the RDMA transport cannot be exercised at all here, and the container-overlay baselines assume a container runtime that is not installed and cannot be apt-installed; network namespaces via unprivileged user namespaces would have to stand in. Repo is marked "[Experimental]" by the author.

title: GPH: An Efficient and Effective Perfect Hashing Scheme for GPU Architectures
note: GPU hash table design with a micro-benchmark and performance model; single GPU

title: GS-Scale: Unlocking Large-Scale 3D Gaussian Splatting Training via Host Offloading
note: Host-offloading 3DGS training explicitly aimed at consumer GPUs; 125 GiB host RAM plus one 24 GB GPU is the intended setting

title: DUCATI: A Dual-Cache Training System for Graph Neural Networks on Giant Graphs with GPU
note: Dual GPU cache (adjacency plus features) with budget allocation for mini-batch GNN training on one GPU - a cache-policy improvement target that fits 24 GB

title: Aster: Enhancing LSM-structures for Scalable Graph Database
note: Graph-oriented LSM key-value storage engine; single machine

title: Can Learned Models Replace Hash Functions?
note: CPU-only study of learned models as hash functions in hash tables and joins; strong reproduce-then-improve target, no GPU or special hardware

title: Prompt Cache: Modular Attention Reuse for Low-Latency Inference
note: Precomputed, reusable attention states for repeated prompt segments - a caching/TTFT problem evaluated on single GPU and even CPU. Small, readable prototype; obvious improvement axes (cache admission/eviction, positional handling). Concern - the schema-based reuse can perturb output quality, so an improvement claim needs an accuracy control.

title: dLoRA: Dynamically Orchestrating Requests and Adapters for LoRA LLM Serving
note: Dynamic merging/unmerging of LoRA adapters and adapter-aware batching - the merge/unmerge mechanism and batching policy are meaningful on one GPU with a 7B base model. Concern - the cross-replica migration part needs multiple GPUs

title: LCP: Enhancing Scientific Data Management with L ossy C ompression for P articles
note: Lossy compressor for particle data; user-space library, CPU

title: Clair Obscur: The Light and Shadow of System Call Interposition - From Pitfalls to Solutions with K23
note: x86-64 system call interposition by binary rewriting; target ISA matches the Threadripper host and the artifact is user space. Also ships a systematic critique of zpoline/lazypoline, so a reproduction fallback is natural. Concern: the hybrid design combines binary rewriting with "multiple Linux interfaces" - if one of those is seccomp user notification it may need CAP_SYS_ADMIN or a no_new_privs path, and ptrace scope is governed by a sysctl this user cannot change. Worth confirming at audit. Repo URL taken from the paper text.

title: STsCache: An Efficient Semantic Caching Scheme for Time-series Data Workloads Based on Hybrid Storage
note: Semantic cache over DRAM plus NVMe SSD with slab management and eviction policies; user-space, single node

title: Eraser: Eliminating Performance Regression on Learned Query Optimizer
note: eliminating performance regressions of learned query optimizers on PostgreSQL

title: IONIA: High-Performance Replication for Modern Disk-based KV Stores
note: Replication protocol exploiting LSM/write-optimized KV-store interface and performance characteristics to get 1-RTT writes and any-replica reads. Concern: it is a distributed protocol normally run on a small cluster. env.md permits emulating distributed behaviour with multiple processes on this host, and 3-5 replica processes over loopback fit easily in 16 cores / 125 GiB; RTT-sensitive latency numbers would be distorted, so a reproduction would need tc-free latency emulation or a focus on the storage-side (background execution, read scalability) claims. No RDMA or special NIC required.

title: Eureka: Enabling Fine-Grained Access and Range Queries on Compressed Scientific Data via Data-Index Co-Compression
note: Data and index co-compression for scientific arrays enabling selective decompression and range queries; user-space compression plus indexing on HPC datasets

title: Skill VM: Write Once, Run Everywhere Efficiently
note: SkVM compiles agent skills against model-harness capability profiles and JIT-solidifies them into code at runtime. Official SJTU-IPADS repo plus a project homepage. Pure user-space runtime. Concern: the evaluation spans eight LLMs and three harnesses, so reproduction is bounded by API cost rather than by hardware.

title: Pruner: A Draft-then-Verify Exploration Mechanism to Accelerate Tensor Program Tuning
note: Draft-then-verify search plus online cost-model adaptation for tensor-program tuning (TVM/Ansor) - single-GPU, and the learned cost model is exactly the kind of component a course project can improve

title: Symbiosis: The Art of Application and Kernel Cache Cooperation
note: Dynamically splits memory between an application cache and the kernel page cache for LevelDB, RocksDB and WiredTiger. Entirely user-space: modified KV stores plus a Python/simpy offline simulator, and memory budgets are enforced with cgroup v2, which env.md delegates to the user slice. No root, no kernel changes, single node. Strong improvement target - the sizing policy is a small, self-contained algorithm.

title: PQCache: Product Quantization-based KVCache for Long Context LLM Inference
note: Product-quantization-based KV cache management for long-context inference; directly on-topic, single GPU

title: Building Bridges: Safe Interactions with Foreign Languages through Omniglot
note: Rust FFI-safety framework; the omniglot-mpk runtime targets ordinary Linux userspace libraries with no root (Rust installs into $HOME). Available + Functional. Concerns: the second half of the evaluation is on the Tock embedded kernel with RISC-V PMP hardware, which is out of reach; and the Linux runtime depends on MPK/PKU availability on an AMD CPU.

title: Grouping Time Series for Efficient Columnar Storage
note: Groups time series to cut columnar timestamp storage overhead - a storage-engine/compression contribution evaluated on a single node. Concern: implementation is reported inside Apache IoTDB but no dedicated artifact repo was confirmed

title: LSM-Raft: Optimizing Raft for LSM-tree Store
note: Raft extension that replicates SSTables instead of raw log entries for LSM stores - storage-engine/replication co-design - concern: replication needs several processes on one host and no repo located

title: MuxTune: Efficient Multi-Task LLM Fine-Tuning in Multi-Tenant Datacenters via Spatial-Temporal Backbone Multiplexing
note: Spatial-temporal multiplexing of a shared backbone across concurrent PEFT fine-tuning tasks - the GPU-underutilization problem it attacks is visible on a single A5000 with small adapters. Concern - evaluated in a multi-tenant multi-GPU datacenter setting and uses NVIDIA Transformer Engine which may want a newer CUDA than driver 535 supports.

title: ALCOP: Automatic Load-Compute Pipelining in Deep Learning Compiler for AI-GPUs
note: Compiler-native multi-stage multi-level load-compute pipelining in TVM plus an analytic performance model for schedule search - entirely single-GPU kernel generation - concern - pinned to an older TVM and CUDA and the pipelining depth assumptions target A100 so Ampere consumer retuning is part of the work

title: Sampling-based Predictive Database Buffer Management
note: Sampling-based predictive buffer replacement evaluated both by simulation on Redshift traces and by patching PostgreSQL; a textbook cache-policy improvement target that fits this machine perfectly

title: Machine Learning Systems are Bloated and Vulnerable
note: MMLB is a user-space measurement and debloating-analysis framework for ML software stacks that quantifies package-level bloat and links it to CVEs; the repo is actively maintained and the analysis itself is plain Python plus vulnerability scanners, which fit the machine easily. Concern: the objects of study are Docker images (TensorFlow/PyTorch/NVIDIA containers) and Docker is not installed and needs root here, so reproduction would require daemonless user-space image tooling (skopeo/umoci/bwrap) to pull and unpack the layers - a real porting risk that the audit stage should weigh.

title: ModelKeeper: Accelerating DNN Training via Automated Training Warmup
note: Training warmup by transforming weights of previously trained models - the matching plus transformation logic is CPU work and warm-started training of small models fits one 24 GB GPU - Concern: the paper uses a large shared cluster and a big model zoo so the zoo and datasets must be scaled down

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of GNN Training Systems: A Data Management Perspective
note: systematic evaluation of GNN training systems from a data-management perspective. Concern: distributed configurations must be dropped

title: The Online Pause and Resume Problem: Optimal Algorithms and An Application to Carbon-Aware Load Shifting
note: A suspend/resume scheduling policy for batch compute workloads, evaluated trace-driven on real grid carbon-intensity traces that ship with the repo - squarely the "policies evaluated with simulators or traces" case, and it runs on CPU in pure Python in minutes. Concern: the core contribution is a competitive-ratio proof for double-threshold algorithms, so the artifact is a numerical simulator rather than a system; an "improvement" here would be algorithmic or an empirical extension (e.g. driving it with real checkpoint/restore costs measured on this machine) rather than a systems build.

title: MLCommons Chakra: Advancing Performance Benchmarking and Co-design using Standardized Execution Traces
note: Open trace schema plus collection/generation/replay tooling with an mlsys26 branch and Zenodo archive; trace analysis and ASTRA-sim style simulation run on one machine. Concerns: the traces themselves come from large production clusters, so any new work here is simulation- or replay-based rather than measured

title: MAC-Attention: a Match--Amend--Complete scheme for fast and accurate attention computation
note: Attention-reuse scheme for long-context decode (match, amend, complete) that composes with paged-KV managers and GQA; model-agnostic and single-GPU. Concern: the 128K-context evaluations need either a small model or host-memory KV offload to fit 24 GB

title: Pittacus: Optimizing LLM Serving on Cloud Data Centers with Forecast Aware Auto-Scaling
note: Forecast-aware autoscaling and routing for LLM serving, evaluated mainly by replaying 10M Microsoft 365 production requests through a simulator plus an ILP. The simulation and forecasting path is CPU-only. Concern: the real-run portion uses multi-region GPU VMs and has no single-node equivalent

title: Accelerating Design Space Exploration for LLM Training Systems with Multi-experiment Parallel Simulation
note: Multiverse is a GPU-accelerated LLM-training simulator; the artifact README explicitly retains CPU-only execution, and the whole workload is simulation, so no real GPU cluster is needed. One A5000 plus 125 GiB RAM is a plausible platform, and simulator throughput/fidelity is an obvious improvement target. Concern: repo is at "Multiverse 2.0" which may have diverged from the NSDI '25 artifact; input traces are Chakra files that must be sourced.

title: MiLo: Efficient Quantized MoE Inference with Mixture of Low-Rank Compensators
note: 3-bit MoE quantization with low-rank compensators and Tensor-Core kernels - Ampere supports the INT-based kernels - concern: Mixtral-8x7B at 3 bits is roughly 20 GB so it only just fits 24 GB and calibration-free quantization still needs large host RAM

title: High-Throughput, Cost-Effective Billion-Scale Vector Search with a Single GPU
note: GPU-centric CPU-assisted on-SSD search engine - the contribution is GPU memory budgeting, PCIe transfer and SSD load balancing - concern: billion-scale corpora need scale-down to fit disk

title: Kishu: Time-Traveling for Computational Notebooks
note: Incremental checkpoint / restore of notebook session state with dedup and CoW-style diffing - a pure user-space checkpointing system. Repo is not cited in the PDF; the official repo is illinoisdata/kishu

title: Anvil: Verifying Liveness of Cluster Management Controllers
note: Verus-based liveness verification of Kubernetes controllers - the proofs and the Rust controllers build and check entirely in user space. Concern - the end-to-end controller experiments assume a Kubernetes cluster and Docker is not installed so that part would need a simulated or unit-test harness

title: CacheCatalyst: Enhancing Web Caching for the Latency-Constrained Internet
note: Web cache revalidation policy - early validation during page load; entirely user-space (browser plus Caddy origin) and trace or emulation driven on one host. Concern - realistic latency effects need network emulation which is available only without root-level tc in some setups.

title: FILM: a Fully Learned Index for Larger-than-Memory Databases
note: Learned index for larger-than-memory data; single node, only RAM plus local disk needed

title: Auxo: Efficient Federated Learning via Scalable Client Clustering
note: Cohort-identification algorithm layered on FedScale; evaluation is trace-driven FL simulation that runs on one GPU. Pure user-space Python/PyTorch. Concern: paper reports large simulated client populations, so a scaled-down client count will be needed to fit 24 GB and 10 weeks. Merge note: scout linked the subdirectory https://github.com/SymbioticLab/FedScale/tree/master/examples/auxo .

title: E2ETune: End-to-End Knob Tuning via Fine-tuned Generative Language Model
note: Fine-tunes a generative language model to emit a whole knob configuration in one shot; Mistral-7B class models fit in 24 GB with parameter-efficient tuning

title: Klotski: Efficient Mixture-of-Expert Inference via Expert-Aware Multi-Batch Pipeline
note: Expert-aware multi-batch pipeline that removes bubbles in offloaded MoE inference - designed for a single memory-constrained GPU; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search (arXiv 2502.06888)

title: sMVX: Multi-Variant Execution on Selected Code Paths
note: In-process monitor plus custom loader, entirely user space, no kernel module and no root; repo builds libmonitor.so / liblmvx.so with plain make and evaluates on user-space server applications. Concern: isolation of the monitor relies on Intel MPK. The Threadripper PRO 5955WX is Zen 3, which does expose protection keys, but the pku CPU flag must be confirmed before committing; without it the MPK path would have to be stubbed or emulated.

title: Dynamic read & write optimization with TurtleKV
note: New on-disk read write balanced TurtleTree structure with explicit write-memory tuning knobs evaluated with YCSB; single-node key-value store

title: Low Rank Learning for Offline Query Optimization
note: Low-rank learning for offline query plan selection; cheap to reproduce on one node

title: Past-Future Scheduler for LLM Serving under SLA Guarantees
note: Peak-memory-aware continuous-batching scheduler using historical output-length distributions - a pure scheduling-policy change inside a serving engine on one GPU; the authors released it inside the LightLLM serving framework

title: Scalable Far Memory: Balancing Faults and Evictions
note: Scope explicitly allows far-memory studied in user space, and this paper implements its three principles in both the Linux kernel *and* a library OS, so the library-OS (user-space) path is the reproducible one. Concerns - the kernel-side half needs root and a custom kernel and is out of reach; the far-memory backend normally needs a second machine or RDMA and would have to be emulated locally; the scalability claims target far higher core counts than 32 threads, so the interesting high-thread regime is partly out of reach.

title: Global Hash Tables Strike Back! An Analysis of Parallel GROUP BY Aggregation
note: Shows a purpose-built concurrent global hash table matches or beats partitioned GROUP BY aggregation in morsel-driven engines; a pure multicore concurrency study

title: AVA: Towards Agentic Video Analytics with Vision Language Models
note: VLM-based agentic video analytics - event knowledge graph indexing plus agentic retrieval; code and the AVA-100 benchmark are both public and the pipeline is built on LMDeploy so a 7-8B VLM fits in 24 GB. Concern - long-video indexing over the full benchmark is compute-heavy and 24 GB limits VLM size.

title: BONES: Near-Optimal Neural-Enhanced Video Streaming
note: A Lyapunov-based controller that jointly schedules a GPU super-resolution enhancement queue against network downloads - a GPU resource manager studied in simulation with real network traces, with code explicitly released in the abstract. Runs on one GPU and CPU-side trace replay. Concern: topic fit is partly video streaming/ABR rather than classic OS scheduling, and the strongest results come from a trace-driven simulator, so a systems improvement would mean strengthening the GPU-side scheduling model (batching, multi-tenant enhancement) rather than the streaming control law.

title: Nested Parquet Is Flat, Why Not Use It? How To Scan Nested Data With On-the-Fly Key Generation and Joins
note: Scanning nested Parquet efficiently in a relational engine; pure user-space file-format work

title: TVM: A Tile-based Video Management Framework
note: tile-based video storage and semantic index that cuts decoded data volume; single machine, GPU used for the DNN oracle

title: FCBench: Cross-Domain Benchmarking of Lossless Compression for Floating-point Data
note: cross-domain lossless floating-point compression benchmark with CPU and GPU codecs. Concern: the roofline analysis uses hardware counters that are blocked here

title: Cardinality Estimation over Knowledge Graphs with Embeddings and Graph Neural Networks
note: GNN plus embedding cardinality estimator for knowledge-graph queries; single GPU. Concern: no artifact found in GitHub search

title: Uncovering Nested Data Parallelism and Data Reuse in DNN Computation with FractalTensor
note: DNN compiler/IR exploiting nested data parallelism; kernels are generated for a single NVIDIA GPU and the artifact builds against CUDA plus cuDNN in user space. Ampere (sm_86) is supported by its CUTLASS/TileFusion-style tiling. Concerns: the AE badge points at https://github.com/microsoft/nnfusion while the maintained code lives in microsoft/FractalTensor and is described as "under active refactoring"; some generated kernels may assume newer CUDA than the 11.8 system nvcc, so a conda CUDA toolkit would be needed.

title: GPEmu: A GPU Emulator for Faster and Cheaper Prototyping and Evaluation of Deep Learning System Research
note: GPU emulator explicitly built so DL-systems research can be prototyped without real GPUs - unusually good fit for a constrained single-GPU machine

title: XProf: An Open, Scalable, and Extensible Profiling System for the Modern ML Stack
note: Open profiler for the OpenXLA stack; host-side trace collection, roofline analysis and the pluggable PJRT profiler API are user-space. Concerns: GPU-side counter collection goes through CUPTI, which NVIDIA restricts to admin users by default, and the paper's value proposition is fleet-scale TPU profiling that cannot be reproduced

title: BGL: GPU-Efficient GNN Training by Optimizing Graph Data I/O and Preprocessing
note: GNN data-loading bottleneck work whose core ideas (feature cache engine plus sampling-order co-design) are a single-GPU-testable caching policy question - Concern: built for multi-GPU multi-node training on billion-edge graphs so it needs scale-down to one GPU and OGB-sized graphs and it pins DGL v0.5.0 which must be built from source

title: GpJSON: High-performance JSON Data Processing on GPUs
note: GPU JSON parser and query library; evaluated on one A100 and works on one A5000. Concern: needs a GraalVM toolchain installed in user space

title: Omni-Paxos: Breaking the Barriers of Partial Connectivity
note: Borderline, kept per the borderline rule. The artifact is a user-space Rust library whose core is deliberately I/O-free and network-agnostic, so a replica group can be run as several processes (or in-process) on one host and partitions can be injected at the transport layer without root. Concern - every headline result in the paper (partial network partitions, reconfiguration I/O at the leader) was measured on a real multi-node cluster, which this machine cannot provide; a project would have to re-frame the claims as simulation.
